ads_ratio.reason: DATA_GAP:ads_ratio - EDGAR diluted share counts (44,065,652 thousand shares for FY2024, Note 23 Earnings Per Share) are in underlying ordinary shares while the Nasdaq price ($10.25) is per ADS; per-share figures must be scaled x30 ordinary shares per ADS to be comparable to the ADS price.
ads_ratio.source: Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, audited consolidated financial statements, Note 1 Description of Business: each CPO represents two series A shares and one series B share of common stock (3 ordinary shares per CPO), and each ADS represents ten CPOs - 30 ordinary shares per ADS. Corroborated in the same statements, Note 21: 662 million own shares cancelled in 2022 were stated as 22.1 million ADSs (662/22.1 is about 30).

moat_against: ROIC proxy only 3.5-9.9% over 2022-2024 (fundamentals.json) and negative in 2020 - returns have not stayed well above the cost of capital through a cycle
Commodity product with no global pricing power: utilization runs the economics, so a small volume drop can erase profit (high operating leverage)
Gross margin has drifted down from about 36% in 2016 to about 33-34% - no expanding pricing-power trend
Energy, carbon (EU ETS/CBAM) and decarbonization capex are structural cost threats; cement is one of the most capital-intensive industries
MXN/USD and multi-currency exposure: a USD-priced ADS on largely non-USD earnings, plus recurring tax/legal overhangs (the Spanish tax assessments that hit 2023)
moat_for: Local market density: cement and aggregates are transport-cost bound (economic radius roughly 200-300km), so plant/quarry positions create local oligopolies
Scarce permitted quarry reserves and capital-intensive plants (over EUR150-200M per 1Mt of capacity) deter new entry
Proven local pricing power: Mexico cement prices rose in local currency in Q2 2026 prints while volumes also grew, and group gross margin has held about 33-34% in 2023-2024
Global scale across Mexico, the US and EMEA plus a ready-mix/aggregates distribution network that pulls through cement volumes
moat_justification: Local cement/aggregates density, quarry and plant scarcity and high transport costs give Cemex pricing power in its core local markets, but the product is a commodity, ROIC has run only about 4-10% through the cycle and gross margin about 31-34%, and earnings ride construction cycles, energy/carbon costs and FX.
name: Cemex, S.A.B. de C.V.
one_liner: BLOCKED (no tier): moat 5/10 local-density cement incumbent - the filing-sourced SBC override (5M FY2024, 20-F Note 22) is in-band but the engine FX-conversion path cannot apply it to 2022-2024 (no MXN rate for USD-translation years), so DATA_GAP:sbc stands; escalated as NEEDS_MAIN_AGENT. ADS ratio 30 applied cleanly; zero-fill base /bin/bash.61/ADS at 0.25 is not scoreable.

sbc_override.reason: DATA_GAP:sbc - SBC missing for fiscal years 2022, 2023 and 2024 of the last 3 under the engine's IFRS tag. The engine applies a single override value to every missing period; $55M is the filed FY2024 figure, and FY2024 is the median year of the 3-year normalized base once SBC is charged (filed series $52M/$61M/$55M), so the base is built from the exact filed figure for its year, with at most a $6M understatement in 2023 (about $0.004 per ordinary share, immaterial against a roughly $0.9-1.3B owner's-earnings base). Amounts are the filer's own filed U.S. dollar figures, the same basis as the engine's filed SBC series for 2015-2021 ($29-77M/yr).
sbc_override.source: Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, audited consolidated financial statements, Note 22 Executive Share-Based Compensation: the combined compensation expense for the Share-Based Compensation Programs amounted to $55 million in 2024, $61 million in 2023 and $52 million in 2022 (statements presented in millions of U.S. dollars)
